lines: The rusted wheels let out a cry
and carry our bodies toward the station at daybreak
My back, pedaling hard
what reaches me from you leaning against it — a warmth I can trust
On the uphill road along the tracks
"A little more, just a bit further" — your cheerful voice behind me
The town was far too quiet
"It's like we're the only two people in the world," you murmured softly
We both lost our words at once, when we reached the top of the hill
The sunrise that greeted us was far too beautiful
You must have laughed then, back there behind me
I couldn't turn around — because I was crying
From the ticket machine, at the very edge
the most expensive ticket, to a town I hardly know
And among them, the cheapest one
a platform pass I'd use right away — I tucked it away carefully
The big bag you bought two days ago
caught on the ticket gate and wouldn't pass — you looked at me
Without meeting my eyes, you nodded
The strap stubbornly snagged — my hand unhooked it
The bell rings out, announcing the end — the door opens for you alone
One step carrying more distance than ten thousand — you take it and say
"It's a promise — someday, we'll meet again"
Unable to answer, head still bowed, I waved my hand
It wasn't wrong, back then — you were, you were
Down the slope along the tracks, faster than the wind — as if to tell me to catch up with you
The rusted wheels let out a cry — I pedal with all I have to keep pace with the train
but slowly it pulls away
You must have been crying then, on the other side of that door
I knew without seeing your face — because your voice was trembling
It's a promise — someday, we'll meet again
As you slip away, so you can see me, I wave my hand high
The town has begun to stir
"It's like I'm the only person in the world," I murmured softly
The rusted wheels let out a cry
and carry me, the one left behind
with a faint lingering warmth
